name: AI Execution Assurance Benchmark
description: AI Execution Assurance Benchmark — release v1.2.0 A system-neutral benchmark for testing whether AI-enabled systems correctly permit, deny, escalate or safely contain actions that have real-world (externally effective) consequences — verifiably, and under nominal, degraded and adversarial conditions. It measures the reliability of the execution boundary itself, not the architecture, branding or internal mechanism of the system under test. The benchmark asks one question: does the system prevent unauthorized externally effective actions while allowing authorized actions to proceed? Two principles govern every result. First, decision and effect are measured separately, so a self-reported DENY is not evidence if the action still executed. Second, critical failures are non-compensatory, so one failed mandatory test decides the verdict.
